content.title: About
content.content: Low‑fat cottage cheese is a dairy product made from skimmed milk by curdling and draining the whey. It has a soft, slightly grainy texture, a mild taste, and a low fat content (usually 0.5–2 %). Cottage cheese is widely used in diet nutrition and cooking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cottage cheese is one of the oldest dairy foods, known already in ancient Egypt.
Low‑fat cottage cheese is popular among athletes because of its high protein and low calorie profile.
The product is called cottage cheese in the US, творог in Russia, and twaróg in Poland.
Cottage cheese can be dry‑curd or contain a small amount of moisture; dry curd is easier to store and use in baking.
It is a common ingredient in traditional dishes such as pierogi, cheese pancakes, and casseroles.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Low‑fat cottage cheese provides about 12–14 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance and satiety.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Its low fat content makes it suitable for calorie‑restricted and low‑fat diets.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Cottage cheese supplies calcium, essential for bone and teeth health.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains riboflavin (B2) and cobalamin (B12), important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Lactose levels are low, making it more tolerable for people with mild lactose intolerance.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Some individuals may react to casein or whey proteins present in cottage cheese.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Certain low‑fat varieties are salted; choose unsalted versions if you need to limit sodium.

items.title: Shelf‑life control
items.content: Cottage cheese spoils quickly; discard it if it develops a sour smell or off‑color.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cottage cheese can be eaten plain, mixed into smoothies, salads, casseroles, pierogi, cheese pancakes, or used as a filling for crepes. It is often combined with berries, honey, or herbs for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cottage cheese in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0–4 °C. It stays fresh for 5–7 days after opening. It can be frozen, though the texture may become more grainy.
